summary: This was an open seat because Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom was term-limited. Xavier Becerra (Democrat) defeated Steve Hilton (Republican) in the top-two general election.

candidates.name: Xavier Becerra
candidates.bio: Xavier Becerra is a Democrat who served as U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services from 2021 to 2025 and as California attorney general from 2017 to 2021. He was first elected to Congress in 1992, represented Los Angeles, and resigned in January 2017.

positions.summary: Says he would declare a state emergency to freeze utility and insurance rates and crack down on price gouging.
Says he would expand state coverage to as many residents as possible and cut insurers' administrative spending.
Says he supports the state's clean energy goals but would revise them if they make energy unaffordable, including the 2035 ban on new gas car sales.

candidates.name: Steve Hilton
candidates.bio: Steve Hilton is a Republican who hosted a weekly Fox News show from 2017 to 2023. He was a senior adviser to British Prime Minister David Cameron from 2010 to 2012.

positions.summary: Says he would deregulate businesses, eliminate the state income tax on the first $150,000 of earnings and halve the gas tax.
Says he would end state-provided Medi-Cal coverage for undocumented immigrants and redirect the money.
Says he wants to overturn the sanctuary law that limits police cooperation with ICE.
Says he would require third graders not reading at grade level to be held back, make it easier to fire teachers and use public funds for private school options in underperforming districts.
Says he would roll back clean energy mandates, end solar and wind purchase requirements and expand natural gas production.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called) Summary originally noted Becerra's share was 59.3% in the AP election-night count, and Hilton's final share was not confirmed. Shares refreshed on November 25, 2026 from The Green Papers (Becerra 8,727,602 and Hilton 4,564,900). Not certified.
